html:
SMTO-EXE-0083 — This clipboard action was already sent or cancelled

GUID: f6044a72-4743-5d40-9d0a-e253f1b3f05a
Slug: clipboard-duplicate
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: clipboard

What happened

  • The Gateway had already received this exact clipboard request, or cancelled it, within the last few minutes, so it refused to run it a second time.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the Conversation, find the earlier clipboard step in this Task and read its result. The first attempt may already have done what you asked.
  2. Paste on the Gateway computer (for example into a blank note) to see what the clipboard holds now. This shows whether the earlier copy or clear really happened.
  3. If the clipboard isn't what you want, send a new message asking SMTO for the change. A new message creates a new request; SMTO won't re-run the old one, so a change is never repeated by accident.

What success looks like

  • The clipboard holds what you wanted, either from the first attempt or from your new request.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep resending the same request; it will be refused again.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway refused to dispatch a clipboard request whose execution ID is already active or in its five-minute finished/cancelled set.

What this means

  • Admission found the execution identity in its active or retained finished/cancelled set and refused to dispatch it again. These operations address the selected Gateway desktop. Metadata discovery does not authorize content reads, and a native control request is not proof of completed effects; retain exact operation and target identities.

Why this can happen

  • Admission found the execution identity in its active or retained finished/cancelled set and refused to dispatch it again.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the original active or retained receipt rather than changing IDs to bypass duplicate protection.

How to fix it

  • Look up the original receipt for that execution_id in the Server and Gateway logs and settle its outcome (clipboard.inspect compares change_id). A repeated execution ID is never re-executed; issue any further action as a distinct, deliberately authorized request instead of reusing or substituting IDs to replay an uncertain effect.
  • Inspect the original receipt and current state; do not reuse or replace identities to replay an uncertain effect.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect the original receipt. Reusing the operation ID will never replay an effect.

How to verify the fix

  • The original operation is settled and any distinct new request is deliberately authorized.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay an uncertain clipboard write or include content in diagnostics.

Technical notes

  • These operations address the selected Gateway desktop. Metadata discovery does not authorize content reads, and a native control request is not proof of completed effects; retain exact operation and target identities.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
